GPU observability stack

A mock multi-region NVIDIA GPU fleet that feeds VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs, shown in Grafana, with Keycloak sign-in, mcp-grafana for AI agents, and a web UI to control it all. Everything runs in containers with one make command.

Features Quick start Control UI Faults Labels API Targets Settings Troubleshooting Changelog

Related guides: Build and deploy Grafana with Docker Compose, Team sync for OAuth in Grafana OSS, Kekaflow chat assistant.

Features

  • Simulates 6 regions, 12 datacenters, and 384 NVIDIA GPUs by default (H100, H200, A100, L40S, and B200 boards).
  • Exports the metrics of NVIDIA's DCGM exporter: utilization, memory, temperature, power, clocks, throttling, Xid, ECC, PCIe, and NVLink.
  • Generates logs from the kernel, DCGM, fabric manager, device plugin, and training, inference, and batch workloads.
  • Uses the same labels on metrics and logs, so you can jump from a series to the logs of the same GPU.
  • Injects faults at any scope, from the whole fleet down to one GPU, with a web UI and a JSON API.
  • Provisions Grafana data sources and the GPU fleet overview dashboard.
  • Adds mcp-grafana so AI agents can query dashboards and data.
  • Includes Keycloak single sign-on with two demo tenants.

Quick start

Start everything: the observability services, Keycloak, Grafana, and mcp-grafana. This reuses the Grafana image. Run make stack-deploy instead to build it first.

make stack-up

To run only VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, and the simulator:

make obs-up
ServiceAddressSign in
Simulator UIhttp://localhost:8090None
Grafanahttp://localhost:3000admin / admin, or Sign in with Keycloak
VictoriaMetricshttp://localhost:8428/vmuiNone
VictoriaLogshttp://localhost:9428/select/vmuiNone
Keycloakhttp://localhost:8080Values in .env
mcp-grafanahttp://localhost:8000/mcpNone

In Grafana, open Dashboards, then GPU fleet, then GPU fleet overview (plugin data source) or GPU fleet overview (Prometheus API), and open both side by side to compare. The first start needs access to grafana.com to install the VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs plugins. Grafana has three data sources: VictoriaMetrics (official plugin, used by the dashboard), VictoriaMetrics (Prometheus API) (for alerting and mcp-grafana), and VictoriaLogs.

Control UI

Open http://localhost:8090. The page refreshes every two seconds.

  • Scenarios: one click applies a preset: healthy, heatwave, training-surge, xid-storm, region-outage, gpu-lost, or chaos.
  • Fleet: pause or resume, reset, set the global load and sensor noise, and resize the fleet (nodes per datacenter and GPUs per node, up to 4096 GPUs).
  • Regions: switch a region off to cut all of its metrics and logs, and set a load multiplier and ambient temperature offset. The table shows GPUs up, utilization, temperature, power, and faulted GPUs.
  • Inject a fault: choose a fault, a scope (region, datacenter, node, GPU), an intensity, and a duration. Active faults are listed with their remaining time and can be removed.
  • Logs: set the background rate and the share of warnings and errors, switch sources on and off, and emit a burst of lines at a scope.
  • Live log tail: filter the generated logs by level and region.

Faults

FaultEffect
thermalCooling failure: GPUs heat up, throttle, and log slowdown warnings.
power_capLimits board power, so power violations grow and clocks drop.
xidXid errors in the kernel log and in DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS. Pick a code or leave it random.
eccSingle-bit errors, and double-bit errors with row remapping above intensity 0.5.
nvlinkCRC and replay errors and lower bandwidth. No effect on boards without NVLink.
pciePCIe replays and a link that retrains at a lower generation or width.
mem_leakFills the framebuffer until the workload logs CUDA out-of-memory errors.
loadPins utilization to a value.
gpu_lostXid 79: the GPU disappears from metrics and the device plugin marks it unhealthy.
node_downThe node stops exporting metrics and logs.

A duration of 0 lasts until you clear the fault.

Fleet and labels

RegionCityGPUDatacenters
us-east-1N. VirginiaH100iad1, iad2
us-west-2OregonH200pdx1, pdx2
eu-west-1IrelandA100dub1, dub2
eu-central-1FrankfurtH100fra1, fra2
ap-south-1MumbaiL40Sbom1, bom2
ap-northeast-1TokyoB200nrt1, nrt2

Metrics and logs share these labels: region, availability_zone, datacenter, cluster, rack, node, gpu, UUID, modelName, and, for GPUs that run a workload, namespace, pod, and container. Logs add app and level, and xid on Xid events.

Examples:

avg by (region) (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL)                  # PromQL, VictoriaMetrics
node:"gpu-iad1-r01-n01" level:in(warn,error)            # LogsQL, VictoriaLogs

Simulator API

The UI uses this JSON API. It has no authentication, so keep the port on your local machine. Invalid input returns status 400 with {"error": "..."}.

MethodPathDescription
GET/api/stateSettings, region aggregates, faults, and log shipping status.
PUT/api/settingsGlobal settings.
PUT/api/regions/{region}enabled, load, ambient_offset.
PUT/api/topologynodes_per_dc, gpus_per_node.
POST/api/faultsInject a fault.
DELETE/api/faults/{id}, /api/faultsRemove one or all faults.
POST/api/logs/burstEmit log lines at once.
POST/api/presets/{name}Apply a preset.
POST/api/resetReboot the fleet and restore defaults.
GET/metrics, /sim/metrics, /healthzPrometheus metrics and health.
 
curl -X POST http://localhost:8090/api/faults \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind": "thermal", "scope": {"region": "eu-west-1", "datacenter": "dub1"}, "duration_s": 900, "intensity": 0.8}'

The full schema is in the documentation.

Connect an AI agent

mcp-grafana listens at http://localhost:8000/mcp. Add it to your MCP client, for example in .cursor/mcp.json:

{ "mcpServers": { "grafana": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" } } }

It signs in as the Grafana admin from .env by default. Set MCP_GRAFANA_TOKEN to use a service account token instead.

obs-logs, obs-down, obs-cleanFollow logs, stop (keep data), stop and delete data.
sim-testRun the simulator unit tests in a container.
stack-upStart everything, reusing the built Grafana image.
stack-deployBuild the Grafana image, then start everything.
stack-testCheck the full stack, including Grafana and mcp-grafana.
stack-ps, stack-logs, stack-downStatus, logs, and stop (keep data).

Settings

Set these in .env. make obs-env appends them with their defaults, and all are optional.

VariableDefaultDescription
OBS_BIND_ADDRESS127.0.0.1Address the simulator, VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, and mcp-grafana ports are published on. None has authentication.
VICTORIAMETRICS_TAG / VICTORIAMETRICS_PORTv1.156.0 / 8428Image tag and host port.
VICTORIALOGS_TAG / VICTORIALOGS_PORTv1.54.0 / 9428Image tag and host port.
OBS_RETENTION7dRetention of metrics and logs.
GPU_SIM_PORT8090Simulator UI and API port.
GPU_SIM_NODES_PER_DC / GPU_SIM_GPUS_PER_NODE4 / 8Fleet size at start.
GPU_SIM_TICK_SECONDS5Seconds between simulation steps.
GPU_SIM_LOG_RATE0.2Background log lines per node per second.
GPU_SIM_SEEDemptyA number makes the simulation repeatable.
MCP_GRAFANA_TAG / MCP_GRAFANA_PORT2.3.0-alpine / 8000Image tag and host port.
MCP_GRAFANA_TOKENemptyGrafana service account token. When empty, the admin user is used.

This stack is for local development and demos. For production Kubernetes deployments, use Helm.

Troubleshooting

  • VictoriaMetrics or VictoriaLogs data source missing: Grafana installs the plugins on start and needs access to grafana.com. Run make stack-logs, look for plugin.installer, then run make stack-up again.
  • Dashboard has no data: wait about 30 seconds after a start, then open http://localhost:8428/targets and check that dcgm-exporter is up.
  • No logs: check ship errors in the simulator header and that Generate logs is on.
  • Port in use: set the matching *_PORT variable in .env.
  • mcp-grafana returns 403: connect through localhost, 127.0.0.1, or mcp-grafana with the configured port.
  • Tenant users see no data sources: provisioning applies to the main organization only.
  • Clean slate: make stack-down, make obs-clean, then make stack-up.

Changelog

  • Added docker-compose.observability.yml with VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, and the GPU simulator (backend/services/gpu-simulator).
  • Added the simulator control UI and API: presets, fault injection at any scope, region switches, and log bursts.
  • Added docker-compose.observability-grafana.yml: provisioned data sources, the GPU fleet overview dashboard, and mcp-grafana.
  • Added the GPU fleet overview (Prometheus API) dashboard, a copy of the main dashboard on the Prometheus-type data source, for side-by-side comparison.
  • Switched the VictoriaMetrics data source and the dashboard to the official victoriametrics-metrics-datasource plugin, and kept a Prometheus-type data source for alerting and mcp-grafana.
  • Added make obs-*, make sim-test, and make stack-* targets, and CI jobs that run the new tests.
